title: Week 42
subtitle: The last week of the range. Induction is usually the plan now.

baby.size: About the size of a watermelon, and still growing
baby.development: The baby is post-term. The skin may be a little dry and the nails long. The baby is ready to be born, and the placenta is the reason not to wait much longer.

you.body: You may be very tired, very uncomfortable, and very ready. Your cervix may be dilated. Contractions may be stronger and more frequent.
you.mind: This is the hardest week for most people. It is not a reflection of anything you did. Ask for help with the waiting, and let people bring food.

coreActions.title: Go in for the induction
coreActions.why: Past 42 weeks the risks of waiting go up for both of you. Induction is the recommended path, and it is a plan rather than an emergency.
coreActions.detail: Bring the bag, the ID, the insurance card, and the car seat. Eat before you go if they let you. Expect it to take a day or more — inductions are slow, especially with a first baby. Ask what the first step is so you know what is happening.

options.label: A scheduled induction
options.detail: You have a date and a time. Bring the bag.

options.label: Go in today
options.detail: If monitoring showed something, go now. Do not wait.

coreActions.skipIf: You are already in labor or already induced.

coreActions.title: Keep every monitoring appointment
coreActions.why: If you are waiting rather than inducing, monitoring is what makes waiting safe. It is the whole reason the wait is allowed.
coreActions.detail: Expect a non-stress test and possibly an ultrasound, twice a week at many practices. If a test looks off, they will talk about induction that day. Do not skip one because you are tired — that is exactly the week not to skip.

options.label: Biophysical profile
options.detail: An ultrasound that scores movement and breathing.

coreActions.skipIf: You are already induced or in labor.

coreActions.title: Tell someone how you are doing
coreActions.why: The last week is isolating. Saying it out loud to one person makes it smaller, and it is the week people most often go quiet.
coreActions.detail: Tell your partner, a friend, or your OB. If you are feeling hopeless or thinking about hurting yourself, call or text 988. That is not an overreaction — it is the right number for that feeling.

options.label: Tell one person
options.detail: A partner, a friend, your OB. Anyone.

options.label: Call or text 988
options.detail: Free, 24 hours, if you are thinking about hurting yourself.

coreActions.skipIf: You are doing well and have people around you.

alsoKnow.title: Post-term is a medical word, not a judgement
alsoKnow.body: It means past 42 weeks. It is common enough that practices have a routine for it. It is not something you caused.

alsoKnow.title: Inductions are slow
alsoKnow.body: A first induction often takes a day or more. Bring something to do, snacks if allowed, and a support person who can stay. It is not an emergency — it is a process.

alsoKnow.title: Movement is still the signal
alsoKnow.body: If the pattern changes, call. Do not wait for the next appointment and do not use a doppler to decide.

redFlags.text: A clear change in your baby's usual movement
Fluid that keeps leaking, or any vaginal bleeding
Thoughts of hurting yourself or ending your life

appointments.label: Induction
appointments.note: Bring the bag, the ID, and the car seat.
